headline: Colorado's Giant Wildlife Bridge Cuts Vehicle Collisions by 91%
meta_description: North America's largest wildlife overpass over I-25 near Larkspur, Colorado has reduced animal-vehicle collisions by 91% in just 10 months, exceeding expectati…
summary_short: A massive 200-foot-wide wildlife overpass near Larkspur, Colorado has slashed collisions between animals and vehicles by 91% in its first 10 months of operation.
body:
A massive infrastructure project spanning 41,800 square feet over Interstate 25 near Larkspur, Colorado is proving that thoughtful design can protect both wildlife and drivers. Ten months after opening in December, North America's largest wildlife overpass has reduced collisions between animals and vehicles by 91%—surpassing the 90% reduction that Colorado Department of Transportation officials had predicted. The bridge measures 200 feet wide and 209 feet long, making it the single largest wildlife crossing structure on the continent. Complementing the main overpass are five underground tunnels for smaller or more timid species, with thousands of yards of fencing guiding animals safely to these crossing points.

The real story here extends beyond safety statistics. A pronghorn antelope was recently videotaped crossing the bridge—the first recorded instance of its kind in 30 years. These naturally migratory animals had been blocked by I-25 for decades; now the overpass is restoring biological pathways that human infrastructure had severed. Meanwhile, drivers below have experienced their own relief: the corridor used to average one collision per day, often causing traffic delays as emergency crews cleared mangled vehicles. That number has plummeted, with traffic delays falling 9% overall.

Perhaps most tellingly, the success has sparked momentum. Colorado Parks and Wildlife spokesperson Bridget O'Rourke noted that "wildlife overpasses and underpasses... it's been statistically proven that it's successful." Six additional locations across Colorado are now being scouted for similar installations, including sites at East Vail Pass between Vail and Copper Mountain, and one specifically designed for Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep. The overpass isn't just about bears and elk anymore—northern leopard frogs, rabbits, and pronghorn antelope are all crossing safely. What started as a single engineering solution is becoming a blueprint for coexistence.
quick_facts: 200 feet wide, 209 feet long wildlife overpass opened December over I-25 near Larkspur, Colorado
91% reduction in animal-vehicle collisions within 10 months of opening
First pronghorn antelope crossing recorded in 30 years
5 underground tunnels complement the main overpass for smaller species
6 additional wildlife crossing locations now being planned across Colorado
